Incorporating the SLOOS, credit conditions look more supportive than the baseline FSR read-through implied. Banks broadly eased standards across residential real estate and consumer categories (including HELOCs and jumbos), eased requirements for credit cards and autos, raised credit card limits, and foreign banks eased CRE standards amid stronger CRE loan demand. Demand was stronger for consumer credit and banks expect stronger demand for C&I and credit cards, though current C&I and auto demand were mixed. This easier supply/firming demand backdrop reinforces the Fed’s cautiously optimistic growth and labor outlook and helps offset tapering headwinds, while FSR-flagged vulnerabilities still cap upside. Net: modestly more positive than before.
